data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts following an explicit checklist will produce more reliable judgments on average than a single expert because the checklist transforms the task from one of high-variance pattern recognition (intuition) to one of low-variance verification (execution).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires the synthesis of non-linear variables not captureable in a discrete list.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'objective verifiability' depends on detecting subtle anomalies that fall outside the checklist's scope (the 'tunnel vision' failure mode ref SCR_007).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist acts as a 'variance-reduction filter' (ref SCR_006) that eliminates 'stupid mistakes'\u2014simple omissions or slips\u2014which are the primary drivers of expert error in objectively verifiable tasks. While the expert has a higher performance ceiling, their reliability is undermined by 'premature closure' (ref SCR_007), whereas the panel's reliability is anchored by a high floor created by the proceduralization of the domain's critical failure points.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
